description: Cargo.lock maintenance updates transitive dependencies. Actions remain pinned by full SHA; custom managers update the exact Rust toolchain and repository gate tools.

packageRules.description: CI's actions, pinned by SHA with the version in a trailing comment. Keep them pinned to a digest rather than letting an update reintroduce a tag reference.

The pull request title becomes the squash commit on main, and this repo's history is conventional and scopeless. Pinned rather than left to the 'auto' default, which infers the convention from history and would produce a title nobody chose.

A crate update changes the binary users install, so it lands as a `fix:` commit (the top-level semanticCommitScope is null, so there is no `(deps)`), a type cocogitto bumps for. A security fix in a dependency then ships with no unrelated feat or fix to carry it. The shipped-path check keeps an Actions or tooling bump, still `chore`, from cutting a release. This rule follows the catch-all above, so it wins.

Lock-file maintenance only moves transitive pins, including Cargo.lock. It stays `chore` and rides along with the next release instead of cutting a patch every week. A vulnerable transitive crate still gets its own `fix:` through the cargo rule above and osvVulnerabilityAlerts.
